lines.line: Summary: A riot-armoured infected found in The Parish campaign. Its front is immune to bullets and blows, so it can only be killed from behind, with fire, with explosions or with the chainsaw.

quoted: The Riot Infected or Riot Guard appears in The Parish campaign.

Riot Infected are immune to bullets, sharp and blunt weaponry such as frying pans if struck from the front. They can only be killed from the back this way, although incendiary and explosive attacks can still kill them as like any other Infected.
Immune to everything but the Chainsaw/Explosions/Flames on the front side.

lines.line: Weak points: Hit it from behind: shove it to stun it and step around it, or shove it off-centre so it spins and shows its back. Fire, explosions and the chainsaw still work from the front.

quoted: Use a melee shove to stun them before moving around them. Sometimes, the melee shove will spin them around, in which case movement isn't required.
The spin shove for exposing a Riot Infected's weak side may be done by not directly shoving them from the center, but from the off-center.
He is vulnerable to flames and explosions.
The Chainsaw is unaffected by his armor.

lines.line: Looks like: An armoured guard in a helmet with a visor and a light blue (sometimes grey) uniform with a sheathed nightstick. The bands on its arm are reflective, so a flashlight picks them out.

quoted: The uniform is either light blue or gray with a sheathed nightstick. (mostly light blue).
If one were to view the helmets of Riot Infected
The visor of the Riot Infected is actually a separate model from the infected model itself.
The bands on the Riot Infected's arm, along with the word "Security" on his chest are reflective
These reflective areas can be easily seen by turning your flashlight on.

lines.line: Tips: Survivor bots cannot tell it from other infected and waste ammo shooting its front, and it is especially dangerous to an incapacitated player, who often cannot land a shot on its back from the floor. Avoid fighting it where it can crawl, because a crawling one cannot be shoved back.

quoted: Survivor Bots are unable to differentiate between Riot Infected and other Infected; they will shoot him even from the front, wasting their ammo.
Riot Infected are particularly dangerous to Incapacitated players, as it is often impossible to land a shot on their backs from the floor.
make sure to not get in a position where they'll be able to crawl, while crawling they're unable to be shoved back, making them much harder to kill.

lines.line: Summary: A common infected in a hazmat suit that is immune to fire and may drop a bile bomb when killed. It has 150 health on Normal and above, and appears in Dead Center's Hotel and Streets, the lower floors of the hospital in No Mercy and Rayford's industrial area in The Sacrifice.

quoted: Immune to flames. Can drop a bile bomb when killed.
150 (Normal, Advanced, Expert, Realism, Survival & Versus)
Dead Center in The Hotel and The Streets. In this game they also appear on the lower floors of the Hospital in No Mercy, and the industrial area of Rayford in the Sacrifice.
Players will occasionally come across Common Infected wearing a hazmat suit

lines.line: Weak points: Fire does nothing to it: a Molotov does not light it and incendiary ammo does not ignite it, though the bullets still hit. Shoot it in the head or hit it with a melee weapon.

quoted: they are resistant to fire, as they do not burst into flames when in the middle of a Molotov's fire, and incendiary ammunition do not set them on fire.
If your primary weapon is loaded with incendiary ammo, it will not light them on fire, but they will still be hit from the bullet.
Shooting them in the head or damaging them with Melee Weapons is encouraged.

lines.line: Looks like: A hazmat suit with a visor, yellow or green (dark blue and white in the No Mercy hospital). The suit has reflective areas, and a bile bomb hangs at its side when it carries one.

quoted: They come in two different varieties: yellow suits and green suits.
These CEDA Workers are dressed in dark blue and white hazmat suits, instead of yellow and green ones.
When shot in the face, blood will splatter across the visor
When killed, there is a chance of them dropping a Bile Bomb (in which case it will be seen strapped to their side).
The CEDA Worker Infected have reflective areas on their suits.

lines.line: Tips: If you have a free slot, pick up the bile bomb from its corpse and keep it for later. In the No Mercy hospital they are nearly the only source of bile bombs in the campaign, but they carry one quite rarely.

quoted: If you have an empty inventory slot, look for the Bile vial on the Agent’s corpse, pick up the Bile, and use it later.
These are the only sources of Bile in the campaign (besides 3 unreliable spawns in the warehouse and one spawn right outside the sewer exit), however they carry Bile quite rarely

lines.line: Summary: A fairground clown found in the Dark Carnival campaign. When it spots survivors it charges, and its squeaky shoes call the infected nearby to join the attack. It has 150 health on Normal and above.

quoted: They wander around the Dark Carnival campaign and when they spot Survivors, they will charge, calling in other Infected with their noisy, squeaky shoes for a mass attack.
an agitated Clown in attack mode attracts Common Infected and other Clown Infected loitering nearby
150 (Normal, Advanced, Expert, Realism, Survival & Versus)

lines.line: Weak points: Any attack that hurts a common infected works on it. Shoving it honks its nose, and after four honks in a row the next shove kills it. If you kill one at a distance, the infected following it stop and mill about for a moment, so shoot them then.

quoted: Although susceptible to all attacks that damage Common Infected
A single Clown Infected's nose can be honked up to four times in succession, as any more shoves will kill the Infected.
If a Clown is killed at a distance, all Infected following him will stop, mill around swatting at the air around his corpse, then attack the Survivors shortly afterwards.
Use this moment to kill them quickly before they realize that you are there.

lines.line: Looks like: Oversized squeaky shoes and bright striped trousers (for example pink and blue, red and yellow, or blue and white), and a flower on its chest that sometimes squirts water.

quoted: Clown pants come in a variety of colors, including pink and blue, red and yellow, blue and white, pink and green and white and red
The flower on the Clown's torso occasionally squirts water.
their choice in oversized footwear
The pants have many different colored stripes

lines.line: Tips: A clown does not make the Director spawn more infected: it only stirs up the ones already nearby, and its pull has no effect during a horde attack. A tight group running in one line behind a clown is easier to shoot than infected arriving from different directions.

quoted: Actually the Clown Infected is just an agitator of the common infected the Director would already spawn normally.
In reality, the effects of the Clown Infected are completely nullified during horde attacks as the horde is programmed to attack the Survivors immediately.

Shooting a tight group of Common Infected running from one direction, following a Clown, is in most cases much easier than sniping them out while they stand around or run at Survivors from different directions.

lines.line: Summary: Infected covered in mud, found in the Swamp Fever campaign and also in the sewers of No Mercy and Death Toll and on The Last Stand's Junkyard map. They sprint on all fours, and a hit from one smears mud across your screen. They have 150 health on Normal and above.

quoted: The Mud Men appear in the campaign Swamp Fever.
the Mud Men now appear in the sewers of No Mercy and Death Toll and The Junkyard map of The Last Stand
Mud Men sprint on all fours low to the ground
A hit from a Mud Man obscures a player's screen with mud
150 (Normal, Advanced, Expert, Realism, Survival & Versus)

lines.line: Weak points: They have the same weaknesses as common infected but a little more health, and they are faster because they move on all fours, so shoot them instead of trying to outrun them. If the mud blurs your view, use a melee weapon.

quoted: They have the same general weaknesses as their common brethren, but are slightly more resistant to damage than them.
Mudmen are faster than Common Infected as they move on all fours, so fire on them instead of attempting to outrun them.
using Melee Weapons if your vision is too blurred to see your team

lines.line: Looks like: A common infected caked in reflective mud that moves low on all fours, though it stands on two legs when idle and stumbles back on two feet when shoved.

quoted: they are covered in mud and use this as camouflage
they stumble back on two feet when shoved. (Moreover, they stand on two legs when idle)
The Mudmen's mud is reflective.

lines.line: Tips: A pipe bomb thrown into the swamp pulls nearby mud men to it and kills them easily, and a bile bomb thrown in gathers them in one spot. Turning off gore in the game's settings also turns off the mud blinding.

quoted: Throwing a pipe bomb into the swamp will drag any of them nearby to the bomb, and it will easily kill them.
Throwing a bile bomb into the swamp can help gather Mud Men in one spot to kill.
Disabling the gore in the settings of the game will also disable the blinding effects from their attacks.

lines.line: Summary: A construction-crew infected with ear protection, a hard hat and a reflective vest, also called Road Crew. They fill the Hard Rain campaign and also appear in the Left 4 Dead 2 versions of No Mercy, Dead Air, The Sacrifice and The Last Stand. They have 150 health on Normal and above.

quoted: Dubbed Worker Infected or Road Crew, these Infected populate the Hard Rain campaign.
They also appear on the Left 4 Dead 2 versions of No Mercy, Dead Air, The Sacrifice and The Last Stand.
Workers are equipped with ear protection, hardhats, and reflective vests
150 (Normal, Advanced, Expert, Realism, Survival & Versus)

lines.line: Weak points: They have the same weaknesses as common infected but a little more health. Their ear protection makes them unable to hear pipe bombs, so a thrown pipe bomb is useless unless it lands near them.

quoted: They have the same general weaknesses as their common brethren, but are slightly more resistant to damage than them.
Their unique ear protectors make them unable to hear pipe bombs.
This projectile is useless unless you aim it so it lands within the vicinity of this zombie type.

lines.line: Looks like: Ear protectors, a yellow or white hard hat and a reflective vest, which is easiest to spot in the storms of Hard Rain.

quoted: Workers are equipped with ear protection, hardhats, and reflective vests which makes them easier to spot in the downpour.
Worker Infected: The hard hat is either yellow or white.
The Worker Infected have reflective vests, which are most noticeable during the storms.

lines.line: Tips: A bile bomb that lands without hitting any infected does not draw them either: they go for the survivors instead, so aim it to hit several infected. They still react to car alarms and to a chainsaw, and they mostly react to movement they see, so you can sneak past one that is looking away.

quoted: If the bile bomb is thrown without hitting any Infected, they will spawn, but will instead attack the Survivors.
Use the bile bomb carefully and try to hit multiple targets with it.
They can still hear car alarms though.
they still react to the sounds of the chainsaw by going after the Survivor with it.
This means they pretty much only react to movement they see.
You can sneak past them if they’re looking the other way

lines.line: Summary: A rare uncommon infected from The Passing, in militia gear with a Molotov, pipe bomb, pills and first aid kit strapped on. It has 1000 health, cannot be set on fire and usually runs away when shot, and killing it can drop some of those items.

quoted: He appears in the DLC campaign The Passing wearing militia attire including a boonie cover and three ammo belts with a strap carrying visible Molotov, Pipe bomb, Pills, and a First Aid Kit.
the Fallen Survivor is actually a "rare" Uncommon Infected
Immune to flames, high health, runs away if provoked in most cases, can drop First Aid/Pipe Bomb/Molotov/Pain Pills when killed.

lines.line: Weak points: A melee weapon kills it in one hit, and so do explosive ammo, the M60 and a headshot while it is still idle; a Magnum body shot does 500 damage. A shove briefly stops it running, but do not rely on shoves alone, because shove fatigue makes you wait three seconds.

quoted: As The Fallen Survivor will run away when shot, use a melee weapon to kill him in a single hit.
The only ways to kill him in one hit are explosive ammunition, melee weapons, the M60, the Heavy Machine Gun, and headshots with any gun while he is idle.
the Magnum does 500 damage on bodyshot on any mode
Melee shoving the Fallen Survivor will temporarily stop his attempts at running away.
shove fatigue will eventually force you to wait three seconds before being able to shove again, giving him an opportunity to escape

lines.line: Looks like: A man in militia clothes with a boonie cover and three ammo belts carrying a Molotov, pipe bomb, pills and first aid kit, in a blue, white or green shirt.

quoted: wearing militia attire including a boonie cover and three ammo belts with a strap carrying visible Molotov
The Fallen Survivor can be wearing a blue, white, or green shirt.

lines.line: Tips: It can carry any of a Molotov, pipe bomb, pain pills and first aid kit, though sometimes only a single Molotov, and it drops them at random when killed. If it runs off it takes a long time to disappear, and the Director tends to generate another one sooner than usual.

quoted: A Fallen Survivor can carry any/all of the following items, which may be randomly dropped upon his death
the Fallen Survivor can spawn carrying as little as only one Molotov cocktail.
While the Fallen Survivor may run and get away, he takes a long time to disappear.
if the Fallen Survivor successfully gets away and despawn, The Director tends to generate another one sooner in the map than it would.

lines.line: Summary: A throwable weapon that sets a large area on fire for about 15 to 17 seconds. The fire spreads over time and burns every infected that touches it, and common infected that run into it burn to cinders.

quoted: The Molotov Cocktail is a throwable weapon that engulfs an area with flames for approximately 15 to 17 seconds. The area of effect is quite large and spreads over time before self-extinguishing. The fire will burn all Infected that come into contact with it. Common Infected who run into the flames will burn to cinders, flailing wildly in the process.

lines.line: Uses: Throw it at a choke point just as a horde reaches it, because infected do not try to avoid fire. On high difficulties keep one for a Tank, which cannot put itself out without water: a burning Tank survives on fire alone for 75 seconds on Easy and Normal, 80 on Advanced and 85 on Expert.

quoted: Infected AI do not attempt to avoid fire in any way.
Try to throw the Molotov just as they reach the choke point in order to increase the likelihood of burning the entire Horde before the flames expire.
It is important in Versus and high campaign difficulties to conserve at least one Molotov for the Tank.
They also can't extinguish themselves (nor can any other ignited Special Infected) unless there is a body of water nearby
A burning Tank will survive by fire alone for 75 seconds on Easy, Normal, Versus and Survival, 80 seconds on Advanced, and 85 seconds on Expert.

lines.line: Tips: It only goes off when it hits the floor, not a wall or a special infected. Do not hit teammates: on Expert even a full-health survivor can die in the flames, and an incapacitated one inside the fire is hard to revive. Water does not seem to put out Molotov fire in Left 4 Dead 2, but it does put out a burning Tank or special infected.

quoted: Throwing a Molotov against a wall does not detonate it; it must hit the floor. This also applies to Special Infected; hitting one directly with a Molotov does not detonate it.

Do not hit teammates. If they are incapacitated inside a fire, it may be difficult to revive them without being incapacitated as well. On Expert difficulty, even Survivors with full health can die from the flames.
it does not seem to affect them at all in Left 4 Dead 2.
However, since water will still extinguish a burning Tank or Special Infected

lines.line: Summary: A throwable bomb with a bright red light and a loudly beeping detector that draws common infected to it, then explodes 6 seconds after it is thrown. The blast is small, a little over three to four metres on Normal, but a well-placed bomb can kill 20 or more at once.

quoted: a bright red LED and loudly beeping smoke detector to attract Common Infected when armed and thrown. Pipe Bombs explode 6 seconds after being thrown.

Its blast radius is relatively small, being confined to little over three to four meters (10 to 13 feet) on the normal difficulty setting; however, since a well-deployed Pipe Bomb is usually tightly surrounded by enemies, as many as 20 or more can be killed at once.

lines.line: Uses: Use it to clear an open area of loosely gathered common infected, keep one for a big horde, or draw enemies away from a teammate who is incapacitated or covered in bile. Do not throw several: common infected run to the first and ignore the others.

quoted: This weapon is perfect for quickly clearing out an open area filled with loosely gathered Common Infected, saving ammo and time.
Keep Pipe Bombs in reserve for dealing with large Hordes.
Deploy a Pipe Bomb to draw enemies away from a teammate who is either incapacitated or covered in Boomer bile.
Do not throw multiple Pipe Bombs. Common Infected will run towards the first one thrown and ignore the others.

lines.line: Tips: Throw it low to the ground, and shove away infected that are already close or they may ignore it. Special infected and worker infected are not drawn to it, and a Witch or Tank near the blast is stumbled but does not chase it.

quoted: Throw Pipe Bombs low to the ground, if possible.
If the Common Infected are too close to you or your allies, they may ignore the Pipe Bomb and attack. Push them away to disengage them so they will chase after the Pipe Bomb.
Special Infected and Uncommon Worker Infected are not attracted to Pipe Bombs.
Witches and Tanks can be stumbled or stunned if a Pipe Bomb explodes near them, but won't chase them.
